6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic

9	/-!
10	# The relative Picard functor of a curve
11	
12	For a scheme `C` over a field `k` (an object of `Over (Spec k)`) this file defines the
13	relative Picard functor of Grothendieck–Kleiman:
14	$$\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}(T) \;=\; \operatorname{Pic}(C \times_k T)\,/\,
15	  \operatorname{Pic}(T),$$
16	line-bundle classes on `C ⊗ T` modulo classes pulled back from the test object `T`
17	along the second projection. The quotient — never the absolute `Pic(C ⊗ T)`, which is
18	not even a separated presheaf in any useful sense — is the functor that étale
19	sheafification and the representability theorem consume.
20	
21	Products are the cartesian-monoidal product of `Over (Spec k)` (chosen pullbacks of
22	schemes): `C ⊗ T`, projection `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`, matching the vocabulary
23	of the challenge statement file.
24	
25	## Main declarations
26	
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase C T`: the subgroup of `(C ⊗ T).left.CechPic` of classes
28	  pulled back from `T` along the second projection.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPic C T`: the relative Picard group, the quotient by
30	  `picFromBase C T`, a `CommGroup`; `relPicMk` is the projection, with
31	  `relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff` the exact coset relation (a genuine range condition, no
32	  choice, no `Nonempty (≅)`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMap C g`: restriction along `g : T' ⟶ T`, descended from
34	  pullback of Čech classes along `C ◁ g`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicFunctor C`: the relative Picard functor
36	  `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat`.
37	-/
38	
39	set_option autoImplicit false
40	
41	universe u
42	
43	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
44	open AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (CechPic)
45	
46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
47	
48	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
49	
50	noncomputable section
51	
52	/-- The subgroup of Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back from the test object `T`
53	along the second projection. The relative Picard group is the quotient by it. -/
54	def picFromBase (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup ((C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :=
55	  (CechPic.map (snd C T).left).range
56	
57	lemma mem_picFromBase_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
58	    L ∈ picFromBase C T ↔ ∃ N : T.left.CechPic, CechPic.map (snd C T).left N = L :=
59	  Iff.rfl
60	
61	/-- The relative Picard group of `C/k` at a test object `T`: Picard classes on `C ⊗ T`
62	modulo classes pulled back from `T`. -/
63	def relPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Type u :=
64	  (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic ⧸ picFromBase C T
65	
66	noncomputable instance (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : CommGroup (relPic C T) :=
67	  QuotientGroup.Quotient.commGroup (picFromBase C T)
68	
69	/-- The projection from Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` to the relative Picard group. -/
70	noncomputable def relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
71	    (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic →* relPic C T :=
72	  QuotientGroup.mk' (picFromBase C T)
73	
74	lemma relPicMk_surjective (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
75	    Function.Surjective (relPicMk C T) :=
76	  QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (picFromBase C T)
77	
78	/-- The exact coset relation: two Picard classes on `C ⊗ T` have equal image in the
79	relative Picard group iff their ratio is pulled back from `T`. -/
80	lemma relPicMk_eq_relPicMk_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
81	    {L L' : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic} :
82	    relPicMk C T L = relPicMk C T L' ↔ L / L' ∈ picFromBase C T :=
83	  QuotientGroup.eq_iff_div_mem
84	
85	@[elab_as_elim]
86	theorem relPic.ind {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {motive : relPic C T → Prop}
87	    (mk : ∀ L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic, motive (relPicMk C T L)) (x : relPic C T) :
88	    motive x :=
89	  QuotientGroup.induction_on x mk
90	
91	variable {T T' T'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
92	
93	/-- Pullback of Čech Picard classes along `C ◁ g` sends classes from `T` to classes
94	from `T'`: the well-definedness of `relPicMap` on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
95	lemma picFromBase_le_comap (g : T' ⟶ T) :
96	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C T').comap (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) := by
97	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
98	  refine ⟨CechPic.map g.left N, ?_⟩
99	  show CechPic.map (snd C T').left (CechPic.map g.left N)
100	      = CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
101	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
102	    ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whiskerLeft_snd]
103	
104	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along `g : T' ⟶ T`: pull back along
105	`C ◁ g` and descend to the quotients. -/
106	noncomputable def relPicMap (g : T' ⟶ T) : relPic C T →* relPic C T' :=
107	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C T')
108	    (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left) (picFromBase_le_comap C g)
109	
110	@[simp]
111	lemma relPicMap_mk (g : T' ⟶ T) (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
112	    relPicMap C g (relPicMk C T L) = relPicMk C T' (CechPic.map (C ◁ g).left L) :=
113	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
114	
115	lemma relPicMap_id (x : relPic C T) : relPicMap C (𝟙 T) x = x := by
116	  induction x using relPic.ind with
117	  | mk L =>
118	    rw [relPicMap_mk, MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_id, Over.id_left,
119	      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]
120	    rfl
121	
122	lemma relPicMap_comp (g : T' ⟶ T) (h : T'' ⟶ T') (x : relPic C T) :
123	    relPicMap C (h ≫ g) x = relPicMap C h (relPicMap C g x) := by
124	  induction x using relPic.ind with
125	  | mk L =>
126	    rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk, relPicMap_mk]
127	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C T'') ?_
128	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
129	      ← MonoidalCategory.whiskerLeft_comp]
130	
131	/-- The relative Picard functor `T ↦ Pic(C ⊗ T)/Pic(T)` of Grothendieck–Kleiman, as a
132	presheaf of commutative groups on `Over (Spec k)`. -/
133	noncomputable def relPicFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
134	  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop)
135	  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMap C g.unop)
136	  map_id T := by
137	    ext x
138	    exact relPicMap_id C x
139	  map_comp g h := by
140	    ext x
141	    exact relPicMap_comp C g.unop h.unop x
142	
143	@[simp]
144	lemma relPicFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
145	    (relPicFunctor C).obj T = CommGrpCat.of (relPic C T.unop) :=
146	  rfl
147	
148	@[simp]
149	lemma relPicFunctor_map {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
150	    (x : relPic C T.unop) :
151	    (relPicFunctor C).map g x = relPicMap C g.unop x :=
152	  rfl
153	
154	/-! ## Naturality in the curve -/
155	
156	variable {C} {C' C'' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
157	
158	/-- Pullback of Čech classes along `g ▷ T` sends classes pulled back from `T` to classes
159	pulled back from `T`: well-definedness of the curve-direction map on the `H_T`-cosets. -/
160	lemma picFromBase_le_comap_whiskerRight (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
161	    picFromBase C T ≤ (picFromBase C' T).comap (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) := by
162	  rintro _ ⟨N, rfl⟩
163	  refine ⟨N, ?_⟩
164	  show CechPic.map (snd C' T).left N
165	      = CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left (CechPic.map (snd C T).left N)
166	  rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,
167	    whiskerRight_snd]
168	
169	/-- Restriction of relative Picard classes along a morphism of curves `g : C' ⟶ C`,
170	at a fixed test object: pull back along `g ▷ T` and descend to the quotients. -/
171	noncomputable def relPicMapCurveApp (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
172	    relPic C T →* relPic C' T :=
173	  QuotientGroup.map (picFromBase C T) (picFromBase C' T)
174	    (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left) (picFromBase_le_comap_whiskerRight g T)
175	
176	@[simp]
177	lemma relPicMapCurveApp_mk (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
178	    (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
179	    relPicMapCurveApp g T (relPicMk C T L)
180	      = relPicMk C' T (CechPic.map (g ▷ T).left L) :=
181	  QuotientGroup.map_mk' _ _ _ _ L
182	
183	/-- Naturality of the relative Picard functor in the curve: a morphism of curves
184	`g : C' ⟶ C` induces a natural transformation `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{C'/k}`. -/
185	noncomputable def relPicMapCurve (g : C' ⟶ C) :
186	    relPicFunctor C ⟶ relPicFunctor C' where
187	  app T := CommGrpCat.ofHom (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop)
188	  naturality T T' t := by
189	    ext x
190	    induction x using relPic.ind with
191	    | mk L =>
192	      show relPicMapCurveApp g T'.unop (relPicMap C t.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
193	          = relPicMap C' t.unop (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
194	      rw [relPicMap_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMap_mk]
195	      refine congrArg (relPicMk C' T'.unop) ?_
196	      rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp,
197	        ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left, ← Over.comp_left, whisker_exchange]
198	
199	@[simp]
200	lemma relPicMapCurve_app_mk (g : C' ⟶ C) (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ)
201	    (L : (C ⊗ T.unop).left.CechPic) :
202	    (relPicMapCurve g).app T (relPicMk C T.unop L)
203	      = relPicMk C' T.unop (CechPic.map (g ▷ T.unop).left L) :=
204	  relPicMapCurveApp_mk g T.unop L
205	
206	/-- The curve-direction maps are strictly functorial: the identity morphism induces the
207	identity transformation. -/
208	lemma relPicMapCurve_id : relPicMapCurve (𝟙 C) = 𝟙 (relPicFunctor C) := by
209	  ext T x
210	  induction x using relPic.ind with
211	  | mk L =>
212	    show relPicMapCurveApp (𝟙 C) T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L) = relPicMk C T.unop L
213	    rw [relPicMapCurveApp_mk, MonoidalCategory.id_whiskerRight, Over.id_left,
214	      Scheme.CechPic.map_id]

218	goes to composition of the induced transformations (contravariantly). -/
219	lemma relPicMapCurve_comp (g' : C'' ⟶ C') (g : C' ⟶ C) :
220	    relPicMapCurve (g' ≫ g) = relPicMapCurve g ≫ relPicMapCurve g' := by

223	  | mk L =>
224	    show relPicMapCurveApp (g' ≫ g) T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L)
225	        = relPicMapCurveApp g' T.unop (relPicMapCurveApp g T.unop (relPicMk C T.unop L))
226	    rw [relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk, relPicMapCurveApp_mk]
227	    refine congrArg (relPicMk C'' T.unop) ?_
228	    rw [← MonoidHom.comp_apply, ← Scheme.CechPic.map_comp, ← Over.comp_left,

10	# THE `∀ T` BINDER OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING IS A STATEMENT ABOUT TEST RINGS
11	
12	Two independent routes to a producer of `(pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy` meet at one
13	hypothesis, and that hypothesis has **no producer** anywhere in the project:
14	
15	  `hvan : ∀ S : Over (Spec k), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C S)`
16	
17	* `Pic0VanishingRoute.jacobianData_of_subsingleton` consumes it and returns a `JacobianData C`
18	  with no atlas, no chart certificate, no coverage and no divisor representability;
19	* `Pic0ChartSeamPairDecided.isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartZero_iff` proves the seam's
20	  *coverage* antecedent at parameter `0` is **equivalent** to it.
21	
22	So `hvan` is not one route's private input; it is where the two routes' costs coincide.
23	
24	**What this file does.** It replaces the `∀ T` quantifier — over all objects of
25	`Over (Spec k)`, i.e. over all `k`-schemes — by a quantifier over commutative `k`-algebras,
26	and it proves the replacement is an **equivalence**, not a sufficient condition.
27	
28	## Why the landed reduction does not already do this
29	
30	`Pic0VanishingRoute` reduces the quantifier for `picEt` (`subsingleton_picEt_of_affine`) and
31	proves that one is an equivalence (`subsingleton_picEtAff_of_forall`).  Its degree-zero
32	consequence `subsingleton_pic0_of_affine` runs **one way only**, and its own docstring says
33	why that is not a repair: the hypothesis is vanishing of the whole `picEt`, which is *strictly
34	stronger* and false at any curve carrying a class of nonzero degree — including `ℙ¹`, where
35	`pic⁰` does vanish.  So the landed chain cannot be applied to the hypothesis anyone needs, in
36	either direction.  The reduction here is for `pic0Subgroup` directly and never mentions
37	`picEt` vanishing.
38	
39	## The mechanism, and why it needed no new mathematics
40	
41	Separation, not gluing.  `Subsingleton` is an equality statement, so only the *ext* half of
42	the descent is used: the affine opens of `T.left` give a morphism-form open cover of `T` by
43	the affine-open test objects `Over.fromSpecAffine T U : overSpec k Γ(T.left, U) ⟶ T`
44	(`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:60`), each an open immersion on the left because
45	`IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` is; and `pic0Subgroup_ext_of_cover`
46	(`Picard/PicEtCoverBridge.lean:342`) says two degree-zero classes agreeing on every member
47	agree.  Under the affine hypothesis each pair of restrictions agrees for free.
48	
49	The `∃!`-gluing bridge in the same file (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`) is *not* used:
50	producing a class from local data would need the compatibility datum, and a subsingleton
51	statement never has to produce anything.  That asymmetry is the whole reason this is cheap
52	where the corresponding representability statement is not.
53	
54	## What the reduced hypothesis is, exactly
55	
56	Three equivalent spellings are given, each strictly more ring-level than the last:
57	
58	1. `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` at every `k`-algebra `A` — the direct form;
59	2. the same transported through `picEtAffineEquiv` to a separation statement about **plus
60	   classes** `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra, with the degree condition read through the
61	   comparison;
62	3. with the field points of `overSpec k A` themselves ring-level: every
63	   `t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A` **is** `Over.overSpecMap φ` for an algebra map
64	   `φ : A →ₐ[k] K` (`exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom`, `Spec.preimage` plus the tower
65	   identity).  So the surviving quantifier in (2) ranges over algebra maps into fields, and no
66	   scheme, open, or morphism of schemes occurs in the hypothesis at all.
67	
68	## What this does NOT do
69	
70	* **It does not prove the vanishing, at any curve.**  It moves the quantifier; the
71	  mathematical content — a computation of the degree-zero relative Picard group of the curve
72	  over an arbitrary test *ring* — is untouched and remains unproduced.  In particular nothing
73	  here discharges `hvan` at `ℙ¹`, where `Curve/P1Curve.lean` supplies the three curve binders
74	  and `Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean` gives `genus (P1.asOver k) = 0`.
75	* **It does not make the hypothesis cheap.**  `infer_instance` fails on
76	  `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` (measured), so the reduced form has content;
77	  the reduction is a change of coordinates on a real obligation, not a discount.
78	* **It says nothing about the atlas route's own residue.**  The coverage clause at
79	  parameter `n > 0` is blocked on a spreading-out (`Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean:221-228`),
80	  which is a different obligation and is not addressed here.
81	
82	## Main declarations
83	
84	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affineOpen_test_mem` — the affine opens of a test give a
85	  morphism-form open cover of it by affine test objects.
86	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_overSpec` — **the reduction**: vanishing at
87	  every affine test gives vanishing at every test.
88	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall` — **the converse**, so the
89	  two are the same hypothesis.
90	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_forall_iff_overSpec` — the equivalence, bundled.
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_algHom_eq_of_overSpec_hom` — every field point of an affine test is
92	  `Spec` of an algebra map, so the field-point quantifier is ring-level too.
93	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_of_picEtAff_sep` — the reduced hypothesis in
94	  plus-class coordinates.
95	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` — **the producer**, with the
96	  quantifier already reduced: a `JacobianData C` from vanishing at affine tests only.
97	-/

210	    [Algebra k A] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k A) :
211	    ∃ phi : A →ₐ[k] K, t = Over.overSpecMap phi := by
212	  have hw : t.left ≫ (overSpec k A).hom = (overSpec k K).hom := Over.w t

214	  have hmap : Spec.map psi = t.left := Spec.map_preimage t.left
215	  have htower : CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A) ≫ psi
216	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K) := by
217	    apply Spec.map_injective
218	    rw [Spec.map_comp, hmap]
219	    exact hw
220	  have hcom : ∀ r : k, psi.hom (algebraMap k A r) = algebraMap k K r := fun r =>
221	    congrArg (fun f => f r) (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom htower)

9	/-!
10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
30	  algebra.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
37	  descent datum.
38	
39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
42	-/

63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft

74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double

77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))

83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x

93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by

105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x

149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
150	  ext
151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]
154	  exact relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
155	
156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
168	    ext y
169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
171	    ext y
172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
180	        rw [hx']
181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]
184	
185	/-- **Refinement-map independence**: any two refinement maps between the same covers
186	transport descent classes identically — what makes the plus construction independent of
187	all choices. -/
188	theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)
192	
193	/-! ## The plus construction -/
194	
195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
197	the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
200	    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2
201	  iseqv := by
202	    constructor
203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,
210	        descentMap_comp, hfg', ← descentMap_comp]
211	
212	variable (A) in
213	/-- The one-step étale plus of the relative Picard functor at the affine test `Spec A`:
214	relative Picard classes on some presented étale cover satisfying the descent condition,
215	modulo agreement on a common refinement.  On affine tests this *is* the étale
216	sheafification of the relative Picard presheaf (one plus suffices because the presheaf is
217	étale-separated — proved separately). -/
218	def PicEtAff : Type u :=
219	  Quotient (picEtAffSetoid C (A := A))
220	
221	namespace PicEtAff
222	
223	/-- The plus class of a relative Picard class with a descent condition on a cover. -/
224	def mk (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) : PicEtAff C A :=
225	  Quotient.mk _ ⟨E, x⟩
226	
227	@[elab_as_elim]
228	theorem ind {motive : PicEtAff C A → Prop}
229	    (mk : ∀ (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E), motive (mk C E x)) :
230	    ∀ q, motive q := by
231	  intro q
232	  induction q using Quotient.ind with
233	  | _ p => exact mk p.1 p.2
234	
235	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {x : descentClasses C E}
236	    {y : descentClasses C F} :
237	    mk C E x = mk C F y ↔
238	      ∃ (G : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier)
239	        (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier), descentMap C f x = descentMap C g y :=
240	  Quotient.eq
241	
242	/-- Transporting the representative to a finer cover does not change the plus class. -/
243	@[simp]
244	theorem mk_descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
245	    (x : descentClasses C E) : mk C F (descentMap C h x) = mk C E x :=
246	  Quotient.sound ⟨F, AlgHom.id A F.Carrier, h, by rw [descentMap_id]⟩
247	
248	/-! ### The group structure -/
249	
250	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the left factor. -/
251	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inl {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
252	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
253	    (x : descentClasses C E) :
254	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x)
255	      = descentMap C f x := by
256	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInl]
257	
258	/-- Transport through a `prodLift` collapses on the right factor. -/
259	lemma descentMap_prodLift_inr {E F H : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
260	    (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier) (g : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] H.Carrier)
261	    (y : descentClasses C F) :
262	    descentMap C (Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift f g) (descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y)
263	      = descentMap C g y := by
264	  rw [← descentMap_comp, Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift_comp_prodInr]
265	
266	set_option maxHeartbeats 4000000 in
267	-- The `rw` chain unifies `descentMap` nests whose `AlgHom` instance arguments run through
268	-- quotient and tensor-product carriers; the unifications are heartbeat-hungry.
269	private lemma mulLift_compat (p q p' q' : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E)
270	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') :
271	    mk C (p.1.prod q.1)
272	        (descentMap C (p.1.prodInl q.1) p.2 * descentMap C (p.1.prodInr q.1) q.2)
273	      = mk C (p'.1.prod q'.1)
274	        (descentMap C (p'.1.prodInl q'.1) p'.2
275	          * descentMap C (p'.1.prodInr q'.1) q'.2) := by
276	  obtain ⟨F, f, f', hf⟩ := hp
277	  obtain ⟨G, g, g', hg⟩ := hq
278	  refine (mk_eq_mk_iff C).mpr ⟨F.prod G,
279	    Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift ((F.prodInl G).comp f) ((F.prodInr G).comp g),
280	    Algebra.EtaleCover.prodLift ((F.prodInl G).comp f') ((F.prodInr G).comp g'), ?_⟩
281	  rw [map_mul, map_mul, descentMap_prodLift_inl, descentMap_prodLift_inr,
282	    descentMap_prodLift_inl, descentMap_prodLift_inr, descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp,
283	    descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hf, hg]
284	
285	instance : Mul (PicEtAff C A) :=
286	  ⟨fun a b => Quotient.liftOn₂ a b
287	    (fun p q => mk C (p.1.prod q.1)
288	      (descentMap C (p.1.prodInl q.1) p.2 * descentMap C (p.1.prodInr q.1) q.2))
289	    fun p q p' q' hp hq => mulLift_compat C p q p' q' hp hq⟩
290	
291	lemma mk_mul_mk (E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E)
292	    (y : descentClasses C F) :
293	    mk C E x * mk C F y
294	      = mk C (E.prod F)
295	          (descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x * descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y) :=
296	  rfl
297	
298	/-- Multiplication of two classes represented on the *same* cover is represented by the
299	product on that cover — the descent condition makes the two transports to the common
300	refinement agree. -/
301	theorem mk_mul_mk_same (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x y : descentClasses C E) :
302	    mk C E x * mk C E y = mk C E (x * y) := by
303	  have h : descentMap C (E.prodInl E) x * descentMap C (E.prodInl E) y
304	      = descentMap C (E.prodInl E) (x * y) :=
305	    (map_mul _ x y).symm
306	  rw [mk_mul_mk, descentMap_congr C (E.prodInr E) (E.prodInl E) y, h, mk_descentMap]
307	
308	instance : One (PicEtAff C A) :=
309	  ⟨mk C (.self A) 1⟩
310	
311	lemma one_def : (1 : PicEtAff C A) = mk C (.self A) 1 :=
312	  rfl
313	
314	/-- The identity class is represented by the identity on every cover. -/
315	theorem mk_one (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) : mk C E 1 = 1 :=
316	  (Quotient.sound ⟨E, AlgHom.id A E.Carrier, E.fromSelf, by
317	    rw [map_one, map_one]⟩ : mk C E 1 = mk C (.self A) 1)
318	
319	private def invSig (p : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) :
320	    Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E :=
321	  ⟨p.1, p.2⁻¹⟩
322	
323	private lemma invSig_compat {p q : Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E}
324	    (h : p ≈ q) : invSig C p ≈ invSig C q := by
325	  obtain ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ := h
326	  have key : descentMap C f p.2⁻¹ = descentMap C g q.2⁻¹ := by
327	    rw [map_inv, map_inv, hfg]
328	  exact ⟨F, f, g, key⟩
329	
330	instance : Inv (PicEtAff C A) :=
331	  ⟨Quotient.map (invSig C) fun _ _ h => invSig_compat C h⟩
332	
333	lemma mk_inv (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
334	    (mk C E x)⁻¹ = mk C E x⁻¹ :=
335	  rfl
336	
337	instance : CommGroup (PicEtAff C A) where
338	  mul_assoc a b c := by
339	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
340	    induction b using ind with | _ F y =>
341	    induction c using ind with | _ G z =>
342	    rw [← mk_descentMap C (((E.prod F).prodInl G).comp (E.prodInl F)) x,
343	      ← mk_descentMap C (((E.prod F).prodInl G).comp (E.prodInr F)) y,
344	      ← mk_descentMap C ((E.prod F).prodInr G) z, mk_mul_mk_same, mk_mul_mk_same,
345	      mk_mul_mk_same, mk_mul_mk_same, mul_assoc]
346	  one_mul a := by
347	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
348	    rw [one_def, mk_mul_mk, map_one, one_mul, mk_descentMap]
349	  mul_one a := by
350	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
351	    rw [one_def, mk_mul_mk, map_one, mul_one, mk_descentMap]
352	  inv_mul_cancel a := by
353	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
354	    rw [mk_inv, mk_mul_mk_same, inv_mul_cancel, mk_one]
355	  mul_comm a b := by
356	    induction a using ind with | _ E x =>
357	    induction b using ind with | _ F y =>
358	    rw [← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInl F) x, ← mk_descentMap C (E.prodInr F) y,
359	      mk_mul_mk_same, mk_mul_mk_same, mul_comm]
360	
361	/-! ### The unit of the plus construction -/
362	
363	/-- Every class pulled back from the base carries the tautological descent datum: the two
364	composites `A → B ⇉ B ⊗[A] B` coincide. -/
365	lemma tautological_mem_descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
366	    (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
367	    relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) x
368	      ∈ descentClasses C E := by
369	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
370	  congr 2
371	  ext a
372	  simp [doubleInl, doubleInr, Algebra.ofId_apply]
373	
374	variable (A) in
375	/-- The unit of the plus construction: a relative Picard class of the affine test,
376	pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological descent datum. -/
377	def unit : relPic C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A where
378	  toFun x := mk C (.self A)
379	    ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) x⟩
380	  map_one' := by
381	    rw [show (⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) 1⟩ :
382	        descentClasses C (.self A)) = 1 from Subtype.ext (map_one _), mk_one]
383	  map_mul' x y := by
384	    rw [show (⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) (x * y)⟩ :
385	        descentClasses C (.self A))
386	        = ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) x⟩
387	          * ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) y⟩ from
388	      Subtype.ext (map_mul _ x y), ← mk_mul_mk_same]
389	
390	end PicEtAff

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle

/-!
# The definitional Picard group: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf

For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:
the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site, computed on **pointed
covers** (one open per point of `X`, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`) and
stabilized along the refinement preorder.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic`: the Picard group `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` as the quotient
  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`, `CechPic.mk_mul_mk_inf`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map`: contravariant functoriality — for
  `f : X ⟶ Y` the pullback `Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic` — with the strict functor laws
  `CechPic.map_id` and `CechPic.map_comp` (the lane keystone).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

namespace Scheme

variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}

/-! ## The Picard group  -/

instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
  iseqv := by
    constructor
    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
      exact ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, e.symm⟩
    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩
      have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
      have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
      simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
      exact e₁'.trans e₂'

/-- The definitional Picard group of a scheme: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf,
stabilized along refinement of pointed covers. -/
def CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
  Quotient (cechPicSetoid X)

namespace CechPic

/-- The Picard class of a unit Čech `H¹` class on a pointed cover. -/
def mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : X.CechPic :=
  ⟦⟨𝒰, a⟩⟧

@[elab_as_elim]
theorem ind {motive : X.CechPic → Prop}
    (mk : ∀ (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰), motive (mk 𝒰 a)) (x : X.CechPic) :
    motive x :=
  Quotient.ind (fun p ↦ by obtain ⟨𝒰, a⟩ := p; exact mk 𝒰 a) x

theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} {a : X.unitsH1 𝒰} {b : X.unitsH1 𝒱} :
    mk 𝒰 a = mk 𝒱 b ↔
      ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱),
        unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b :=
  Quotient.eq

/-- Two classes agreeing after restriction to a common refinement are equal; in
particular `mk` is invariant under restriction. -/
@[simp]
theorem mk_unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
    mk 𝒱 (unitsRes h a) = mk 𝒰 a :=
  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒱, le_rfl, h, unitsRes_rfl _⟩

private def mulSig (p q : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
  ⟨p.1 ⊓ q.1, unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2⟩

private lemma mulSig_assoc {𝒰 𝒱 𝒳 : X.PointedCover} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) (b : X.unitsH1 𝒱)
    (c : X.unitsH1 𝒳) :
    mk (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳)
        (unitsRes inf_le_left (unitsRes inf_le_left a * unitsRes inf_le_right b) *
          unitsRes inf_le_right c)
      = mk (𝒰 ⊓ (𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳))
        (unitsRes inf_le_left a *
          unitsRes inf_le_right (unitsRes inf_le_left b * unitsRes inf_le_right c)) := by
  refine mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ⟨𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱 ⊓ 𝒳, le_rfl, (inf_assoc 𝒰 𝒱 𝒳).le, ?_⟩
  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes, unitsRes_rfl]
  exact mul_assoc _ _ _

private lemma mulSig_compat {p p' q q' : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰}
    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') : mulSig p q ≈ mulSig p' q' := by
  obtain ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ := hp
  obtain ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩ := hq
  have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
  have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
  simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
  refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_inf h₁ h₃, inf_le_inf h₂ h₄, ?_⟩
  show unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₁ h₃) (unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2)
      = unitsRes (inf_le_inf h₂ h₄) (unitsRes inf_le_left p'.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q'.2)
  simp only [map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes]
  rw [e₁', e₂']

instance : CommGroup X.CechPic where
  mul := Quotient.map₂ mulSig (fun _ _ hp _ _ hq ↦ mulSig_compat hp hq)
  one := mk ⊤ 1
  inv := Quotient.map (fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, p.2⁻¹⟩) (by
    rintro p p' ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
    exact ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, by simp only [map_inv, e]⟩)
  mul_assoc a b c := by
    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
    induction b using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒱 b =>
    induction c using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒳 c =>
    exact mulSig_assoc a b c
  one_mul a := by
    induction a using CechPic.ind with | _ 𝒰 a =>
    show mk (⊤ ⊓ 𝒰) (unitsRes inf_le_left (1 : X.unitsH1 ⊤) * unitsRes inf_le_right a)
      = mk 𝒰 a
    rw [map_one, one_mul, mk_unitsRes]
  mul_one a := by

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSections
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtAffMap

/-!
# The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor on all test objects: the object level

For a curve `C` over `k`, the étale-sheafified relative Picard group of an **affine**
test is the one-step plus construction `PicEtAff C A` (étale-separatedness of the
relative Picard presheaf makes one plus suffice — axiom (C1),
`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CechKernelLemma`).  The frozen group-object interface forces
the functor to exist on **all** of `Over (Spec k)`; following the resolution of the
Layer-2 vehicle question (inbox I-0140), the extension is the *bespoke affine-opens
limit*: a section over a test object `T` is a compatible family of plus classes over the
affine opens of `T.left`, valued in `PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U)` via the section-ring
algebras of `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtSections`.  The index poset is `Type u`-small,
which is the point of the vehicle.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEt C T`: the limit, as the subgroup of the product over
  `T.left.affineOpens` cut out by compatibility under restriction, with its `CommGroup`
  structure; `picEt.eval` is evaluation at an affine open.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.congr C e`: transport of plus classes along an isomorphism
  of test algebras.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.picEtAffineEquiv C A`: **the affine comparison** — on an affine
  test `overSpec k A`, evaluation at the top affine open is a group isomorphism
  `picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A` (the affine-opens poset of an affine test has
  a terminal element, so the limit collapses).

Functoriality in `T` — restriction along an arbitrary morphism of test objects, by
gluing over basic-open refinements, licensed by (C1)-separatedness — is built on top of
the Zariski sheaf property of `PicEtAff` in `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtMap`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra

noncomputable section

/-! ## Transport of plus classes along an isomorphism of test algebras -/

namespace PicEtAff

variable {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

/-- Transport of étale-plus Picard classes along an isomorphism of test algebras. -/
def congr (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) : PicEtAff C A ≃* PicEtAff C B where
  toFun := mapAlg C e.toAlgHom
  invFun := mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom
  left_inv x := by
    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.symm.toAlgHom.comp e.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k A from
      AlgHom.ext fun a => e.symm_apply_apply a]
    exact mapAlg_id C x
  right_inv x := by
    rw [← mapAlg_comp, show (e.toAlgHom.comp e.symm.toAlgHom) = AlgHom.id k B from
      AlgHom.ext fun b => e.apply_symm_apply b]
    exact mapAlg_id C x
  map_mul' x y := map_mul (mapAlg C e.toAlgHom) x y

@[simp]
lemma congr_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C A) :
    congr C e x = mapAlg C e.toAlgHom x :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma congr_symm_apply (e : A ≃ₐ[k] B) (x : PicEtAff C B) :
    (congr C e).symm x = mapAlg C e.symm.toAlgHom x :=
  rfl

end PicEtAff

/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/

variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))

/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
def picEtSubgroup :
    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]

/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
def picEt : Type u :=
  picEtSubgroup C T

noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))

namespace picEt

variable {C T}

/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
  s.2 U V h

@[ext]
lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
  Subtype.ext (funext h)

variable (C T) in
/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype

@[simp]
lemma eval_apply (U : T.left.affineOpens) (s : picEt C T) : eval C T U s = s.1 U :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma mul_val (s t : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
    (s * t).1 U = s.1 U * t.1 U :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma one_val (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (1 : picEt C T).1 U = 1 :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma inv_val (s : picEt C T) (U : T.left.affineOpens) : (s⁻¹).1 U = (s.1 U)⁻¹ :=
  rfl

end picEt

/-! ## The affine comparison -/

section Affine

variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]

/-- The top affine open of an affine test object. -/
def overSpecTopAffine : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens :=
  ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top_overSpec k A⟩

/-- Evaluation at the top affine open of an affine test, composed with the
`ΓSpecIso`-transport into the test algebra: the forward direction of the affine
comparison. -/
def picEtToAff : picEt C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A :=
  (PicEtAff.congr C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A)).toMonoidHom.comp
    (picEt.eval C (overSpec k A) (overSpecTopAffine A))

lemma picEtToAff_apply (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
    picEtToAff C A s
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
  rfl

/-- The section of `picEt` over an affine test determined by a plus class of the test
algebra: restrict from the top affine open — the inverse direction of the affine
comparison. -/
def picEtOfAff : PicEtAff C A →* picEt C (overSpec k A) where
  toFun x :=
    ⟨fun U => PicEtAff.mapAlg C
      ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
        (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x,
      fun U V h => by rw [← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp, ← AlgHom.comp_assoc,
        Over.resAlgHom_comp]⟩
  map_one' := picEt.ext fun U => map_one (PicEtAff.mapAlg C _)
  map_mul' x y := picEt.ext fun U => map_mul (PicEtAff.mapAlg C _) x y

lemma picEtOfAff_val (x : PicEtAff C A) (U : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens) :
    (picEtOfAff C A x).1 U
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x :=
  rfl

private lemma picEtOfAff_comp_picEtToAff :
    (picEtOfAff C A).comp (picEtToAff C A) = MonoidHom.id (picEt C (overSpec k A)) := by
  refine MonoidHom.ext fun s => picEt.ext fun U => ?_
  calc ((picEtOfAff C A) (picEtToAff C A s)).1 U
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
          (((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom).comp
            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom)
          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
        (PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp C _ _ _).symm
    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top)
          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) := by
        rw [AlgHom.comp_assoc,
          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom.comp
              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k A).left, ⊤) from
            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm_apply_apply a,
          AlgHom.comp_id]
    _ = s.1 U := s.compat U (overSpecTopAffine A) le_top

private lemma picEtToAff_comp_picEtOfAff :
    (picEtToAff C A).comp (picEtOfAff C A) = MonoidHom.id (PicEtAff C A) := by
  refine MonoidHom.ext fun x => ?_
  calc (picEtToAff C A) (picEtOfAff C A x)
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
          ((Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom.comp
            ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom)) x :=
        (PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp C _ _ _).symm
    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (AlgHom.id k A) x := by
        rw [show Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) (le_top :
              (⊤ : (overSpec k A).left.Opens) ≤ (⊤ : (overSpec k A).left.Opens))
            = AlgHom.id k Γ((overSpec k A).left, ⊤) from Over.resAlgHom_rfl _ le_top,
          AlgHom.id_comp,
          show (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom.comp
              (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom
            = AlgHom.id k A from
            AlgHom.ext fun a => (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).apply_symm_apply a]
    _ = x := PicEtAff.mapAlg_id C x

/-- **The affine comparison isomorphism**: on an affine test `overSpec k A`, the
affine-opens limit `picEt` collapses by evaluation at the terminal element `⊤` of the
affine-opens poset to the one-step plus `PicEtAff C A` of the test algebra. -/
def picEtAffineEquiv : picEt C (overSpec k A) ≃* PicEtAff C A :=
  MonoidHom.toMulEquiv (picEtToAff C A) (picEtOfAff C A)
    (picEtOfAff_comp_picEtToAff C A) (picEtToAff_comp_picEtOfAff C A)

@[simp]
lemma picEtAffineEquiv_apply (s : picEt C (overSpec k A)) :
    picEtAffineEquiv C A s
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).toAlgHom
          (s.1 (overSpecTopAffine A)) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma picEtAffineEquiv_symm_apply_val (x : PicEtAff C A)
    (U : (overSpec k A).left.affineOpens) :
    ((picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm x).1 U
      = PicEtAff.mapAlg C
          ((Over.resAlgHom (overSpec k A) le_top).comp
            (Over.overSpecΓTopAlgEquiv k A).symm.toAlgHom) x :=
  rfl

end Affine

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The degree at a field point -/

/-- **The degree of an étale Picard class at a field point** (gap G-D6): restrict along
`t : overSpec k K ⟶ T`, collapse by the affine comparison to a plus class of the test
algebra `K`, and take its degree (SB-6).  Well-defined in the representative of the
restricted class by the zigzag (WD) underlying `PicEtAff.degAff`. -/
def degAt {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) {K : Type u} [Field K]
    [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : ℤ :=
  PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))

section DegAt

variable {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- The trivial class has degree zero at every field point. -/
@[simp]
theorem degAt_one (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) : degAt (1 : picEt C T) t = 0 := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t 1)) = 0
  rw [map_one, map_one, PicEtAff.degAff_one]

/-- The degree at a field point of a product of classes is the sum of the degrees. -/
theorem degAt_mul (lam mu : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :
    degAt (lam * mu) t = degAt lam t + degAt mu t := by
  change PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t (lam * mu)))
      = PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
        + PicEtAff.degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t mu))
  rw [map_mul, map_mul, PicEtAff.degAff_mul]

/-- The degree at a field point of an inverse class is the negation of the degree. -/
theorem degAt_inv (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T) :

namespace CechPic

variable (X) [IsAffine X]

/-- **Surjectivity of the Čech–Picard descent homomorphism**: every class of invertible
modules over the global sections arises from a unit Čech cocycle on a trivializing
pointed cover. -/
theorem toPic_surjective : Function.Surjective (toPic X) := by
  intro c
  obtain ⟨F⟩ := TrivializingFamily.nonempty (X := X) (N := c.AsModule)
  obtain ⟨P⟩ := PointedCover.BasicRefinement.nonempty F.cover
  refine ⟨CechPic.mk F.cover (OneCocycle.class F.cocycle), ?_⟩
  rw [toPic_mk F.cover F.cocycle P, F.pic_cocycle P, CommRing.Pic.mk_eq_self]

/-- The Čech–Picard descent homomorphism of an affine scheme is an isomorphism. -/
theorem toPic_bijective : Function.Bijective (toPic X) :=
  ⟨toPic_injective, toPic_surjective X⟩

end CechPic

/-- **The Čech–Picard dictionary** of an affine scheme: the definitional Čech Picard
group on pointed Zariski covers is mathlib's Picard group of invertible modules over
the global sections. -/
noncomputable def cechPicEquivPic (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    X.CechPic ≃* CommRing.Pic Γ(X, ⊤) :=
  MulEquiv.ofBijective (CechPic.toPic X) (CechPic.toPic_bijective X)

@[simp]
lemma cechPicEquivPic_apply (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (c : X.CechPic) :
    cechPicEquivPic X c = CechPic.toPic X c :=
  rfl

end Scheme

# The two-chart Čech `Ȟ¹` of units embeds in the Picard group (W5-T4 clause (iii-a)/(iii-b))

For a scheme `X` with two opens `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`, the two-chart Čech cohomology of units

```
Ȟ¹(V₀,V₁ ; 𝒪ˣ)  =  Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ ⧸ (im Γ(V₀)ˣ · im Γ(V₁)ˣ)
```

maps to the definitional Picard group `X.CechPic`, **injectively**
(`Scheme.twoChartClass_injective`). This file builds that map and proves the injectivity.

## Why this file exists: clauses (iii-a) and (iii-b), which are not about dual numbers

`informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` §6 splits the Wave-5 residue "clause (iii)" — the last input to
the Kleiman §5 Thm. 5.11 dimension identity — into three parts, and observes that **two of
them contain no dual numbers, no curves and no `H¹`**. Those two are exactly this file:

* **(iii-a)** the comparison homomorphism `twoChartClass` exists;
* **(iii-b)** it is injective.

Both are general statements about a scheme with a two-open cover, so they are stated here at
that generality rather than at `C ×_k Spec k[ε]`. The remaining part, **(iii-c)**
(surjectivity onto the `ε`-kernel), is the only one that needs the thickening; it consumes
`DualNumber.free_of_cyclic_mod_eps` and lives elsewhere.

The two-chart Čech quotient here is the **same carrier** the truncated-exponential engine of
`Tangent/TruncExpCech.lean` computes: `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits` of the two restriction
maps. So `twoChartClass` is precisely the arrow that connects the (landed) T2 engine to the
(definitional) Picard group, in the direction the tangent computation needs.

## Implementation notes

`CechPic` is built on **pointed** covers — one open per point — so a two-open cover enters
through a selector `sel : X → Bool` with `x ∈ V (sel x)`, exactly as
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.pieceIndex` and `thetaFieldChartIndex` do elsewhere in the tree.
Indexing the charts by `Bool` (rather than by two named opens) is what makes the cocycle law a
`cases`-bash that closes uniformly.

The cocycle attached to an overlap unit `u` has pair values `1` on the diagonal, `u` at
`(0,1)` and the `inf_comm`-transport of `u⁻¹` at `(1,0)` (`Scheme.twoChartPairUnit`).

**A negative result, recorded so it is not retried** (worksheet §6.2): the slick spelling
`pairUnit s t = u ^ (δ t − δ s)`, which would close the cocycle law by `zpow_add` alone, does
**not** typecheck. On the diagonal the ambient open `T` need only be `≤ V s`, where `u` — a
section on `V₀ ⊓ V₁` — cannot be restricted at all. The exponent trick needs a unit on the
union and there is none. The eight-case `cases` bash is the honest route, and it is three
lines.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartCover` — the pointed cover of a selector.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.twoChartCocycle` — the unit Čech 1-cocycle of an overlap unit.
